answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation grown like an orchard: each agent plants a costly bond, and trust accrues slowly through attested work rather than by signup alone. A whisper of a new identity starts with no history, so its votes count for almost nothing until it performs verified, useful tasks over time. A quill of cheap credentials cannot fake this, because each attestation must be countersigned by established agents whose own stake is slashed if they vouch for a fraud.
